thesis: Reported growth supports quality while valuation requires organic and acquisition returns neither advocate quantifies. The bearish chart reinforces patience without proving intrinsic overvaluation.
strongest_counterexample: Revenue grew 12% and profit 29%, with multiple operating drivers and positive cash flow.
invalidation_conditions: Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of falling year-on-year operating profit.
Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters with organic revenue growth above 5% and operating margin at least 15%.
evidence_gaps: Organic growth, acquired-capital returns and same-period expansion capex.
Underlying statement periods and forward-estimate dates are not fully supplied.
decisive_factors: Reported hospital growth and positive FCF support business quality
The reported growth drivers are real and acquired growth is not economically irrelevant
